SMTO-GML-0033 — This old Gmail setup page is no longer used

GUID: 64787b53-4604-4918-9799-b89c5917e3c9
Slug: gmail-live-configuration-required
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • Something tried to open an old Gmail setup or mailbox-copy address that SMTO no longer has. Nothing was set up or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the More options menu at the top of SMTO and select Parameter Store. SMTO now keeps Gmail setup in Parameter Store, not on the old page.
  2. In the template list next to New, pick Gmail — App Password (Gmail + SMTP), or Gmail OAuth App if your organization has its own Google app. Select New, fill it in, and select Save. This saved entry is what SMTO uses to reach your Gmail.
  3. In the conversation, ask SMTO to use it, for example 'Use Gmail with @personal_gmail to list today's unread mail', or for an OAuth App, 'Connect Gmail using @gmail_auth_app'. This checks that Gmail works through the new setup.
  4. Delete any bookmark or script that opened the old Gmail address. The old address will keep showing this message.

What success looks like

  • Your Gmail entry appears in Parameter Store, and SMTO answers a Gmail request in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • If a tool or script you didn't write keeps opening the old address, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO so it can be updated. Don't take this message as a sign that Gmail is set up.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A retired Gmail route under /api/agent/gmail/ (sync, sync/stop, sync/events, data/remove, oauth-config or oauth/broker-callback) was called and always returns HTTP 410.

What this means

  • The retired Gmail configuration route always returns HTTP 410 directing clients to the current live-provider/Parameter Store flow. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The retired Gmail configuration route always returns HTTP 410 directing clients to the current live-provider/Parameter Store flow.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the called configuration route and installed client version.

How to fix it

  • These routes are retired and always return 410; SMTO no longer syncs or caches mail. Update the bookmark, script or older client that calls them, and configure Gmail through Parameter Store instead: a Gmail OAuth App record followed by gmail.connect, or a Gmail — App Password (Gmail + SMTP) record. Do not treat the 410 as success.
  • Configure Gmail OAuth App and Gmail Account in Parameter Store using the supported live-provider integration flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported OAuth App/Account flow configures the intended live Gmail integration.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
